meta.title: Fish Supply for Importers and Distributors
meta.description: How to source fresh fish from AZAFCO: send your specification, we review supply, then quote packing, shipping and documents. Start an RFQ.

hero.title: A clear procurement path from enquiry to quotation
hero.intro: Tell us the specification. We evaluate supply, packing and commercial terms, then reply with the next steps.

serve.title: Built for professional buyers
serve.intro: We supply businesses, not consumers. Each buyer type has its own questions, so we answer them in the quotation.

items.title: Seafood importers
items.text: Species, sizes, packing and volumes matched to your market.

items.title: Wholesalers and distributors
items.text: Clear grading, weights, packing and delivery terms in the quote.

items.title: Hotels, restaurants and catering
items.text: Consistent quality, a documented process and a direct contact.

items.title: Foodservice suppliers
items.text: Recurring supply discussed against capacity and your programme.

process.title: Four steps from specification to coordination

steps.title: Send your requirement
steps.text: Company, country, business type, species, size grade, product form, expected quantity, packing and delivery date.

steps.title: Technical and commercial review
steps.text: We review the product, availability, our ability to meet the specification, market requirements and the relevant export documents.

steps.title: A clear quotation
steps.text: Issued on confirmed data: price and its terms, quantity, packing, offer validity, shipping and the expected schedule.

steps.title: Coordination and delivery
steps.text: After agreement and contract, both sides coordinate operations, delivery and documents.

prepare.title: What to prepare
prepare.intro: A complete requirement gets a more useful first reply.

terms.title: Confirmed per quotation, not promised in advance
terms.intro: We do not publish price lists or blanket terms. These points are set in each formal quotation:

items.title: Price
items.text: Depends on species, grade, volume, packing and delivery terms.

items.title: Availability
items.text: Confirmed against current supply when we review your request.

items.title: Documents
items.text: The list and scope are confirmed for your destination.

items.title: Incoterms
items.text: Agreed in the quotation and contract.

items.title: Products
items.text: Species pages with what can be confirmed per product.

items.title: Processing and packing
items.text: How fish is handled, packed and dispatched.

items.title: Export markets
items.text: Current markets and how each destination is handled.

faq.title: Questions buyers ask before an RFQ

items.q: What is the minimum order quantity?
items.a: It varies by species and terms. Send your expected volume and we confirm what is possible in the quotation.

items.q: Which sizes and grades can you supply?
items.a: Sizes depend on the species and on current supply. Tell us your grade or grading specification, and we confirm what we can meet.
Fresh fish is packed in insulated EPS boxes with ice. Other packing formats or your own specification are reviewed per product and requirement.

items.q: Can you pack under our label?
items.a: It is reviewed per product and requirement. Include your label requirements in the RFQ notes.

items.q: Which quality documents and certificates are available?
items.a: The list and scope are confirmed when we review your request, for your product and destination.
Chilled, by air freight or by road depending on the destination. The transport mode is confirmed in the quotation; we do not publish fixed transit times.

items.q: Do you accept recurring supply programmes?
items.a: Yes, they can be discussed based on capacity and your needs. Tell us the frequency you expect.

items.q: When will I receive a quotation?
items.a: It depends on how complete the specification is and on current availability. We first review the request, then contact you to confirm the details before a formal quotation.

rfq.title: Start your RFQ
rfq.intro: Two short steps. Nothing is binding until a formal quotation is agreed.
